It finds that tariffs at 25 percent would decrease U.S. GDP growth by 0.18 percent in the initial year, and if sustained, would lead to 0.76 percent less GDP growth in the 10th year post-implementation than would otherwise be the case. results.title: Section 232 Automotive Tariffs: Issues for Congress
results.content: In 2025, President Donald Trump imposed 25% tariffs on U.S. imports of automobiles and certain automobile parts under Section 232. Section 232 authorizes the President to take action (e.g., tariffs, quotas, or negotiations) if the Secretary of Commerce determines that imports of a good "threaten to impair" U.S. national security. President Trump imposed auto tariffs based on the findings of a 2019 investigation, which concluded that U.S. auto imports were a threat to U.S. national security. [...] face a 15% total tariff.
